entries.comment: Prime 3: Berserker Lords and Berserker Knights
entries.content:
Berserkers are the Phazon-saturated heavy troops the Space Pirates fielded during the Phazon crisis (Metroid Prime 3: Corruption), Pirates mutated by Phazon far beyond the regular ranks. Like the Elite Pirates and the Omega Pirate of Project Helix before them, they are soldiers remade by Phazon.

Berserker Knights are the common grade. Samus's logbook called the Knight a shocking example of how far the Pirates will go for dominance: heavily mutated, nearly mindless and "driven by battle lust." Berserker Lords are Knights pushed further. Only the few Knights that survive the most extreme corruption are promoted to Lord, and the logbook judged Lords "a desperate measure, designed to exploit Phazon as much as possible." A Lord is far more resistant to damage than a Knight, marked by ornate Phazite plating and the Phazon reserves it carries on its back.

Both grades fight with ground shock waves and orbs of Phazon, and both wear Phazite plating over the head that ordinary fire cannot harm; it can be broken only by the projectiles the Berserker itself fires. Samus had to shoot each Phazon orb back into its maker until the plating shattered and the head lay open. Until then a Lord's shoulders were the only unprotected area vulnerable to standard weapons. Phazon-based attacks hurt Knights, and late in the crisis the Nova Beam, aimed with the X-Ray Visor, struck through the plating directly.

Encounters:
- A Berserker Lord in Docking Bay 5 of the G.F.S. Olympus, met during the Pirate boarding raid, delayed Samus's departure for Norion.
- On Norion, Ghor made quick work of a Berserker Knight to clear the path to Generator C.
- Samus first scanned a Knight in the Ancient Courtyard of Bryyo Thorn Jungle.
- A second Lord held the Turbine Chamber of SkyTown on Elysia, where the first component of the Theronian Bomb lay.
- Knights defended Pirate Command on the Pirate Homeworld.
- On the Homeworld the corrupted Gandrayda took a Berserker Knight's form, using Phazon-charged versions of its attacks and inheriting its weaknesses.
entries.notes: 339 words. The Lord logbook is quoted verbatim from Metroid Wiki: shoulders 'only unprotected area', head plating 'can only be destroyed by the projectiles it fires', 'desperate measure', promotion, ornate plating and back-mounted Phazon reserves. Lord first location 'G.F.S. Olympus - Docking Bay 5' comes from the logbook infobox. The 'highest level of corruption' quote is paraphrased as 'most extreme corruption' to keep the banned word 'level' out of content. The Knight logbook ('nearly mindless', 'driven by battle lust', 'shocking example') comes from the Metroid Wiki summary, so only 'driven by battle lust' is quoted. The Turbine Chamber Lord and the first Theronian Bomb component are confirmed by the Metroid Wiki Metroid Prime 3 page and the Berserker Lord rewards. The 'eastern SkyTown' placement appeared only in a Wikitroid search snippet, so it was left out. The Project Helix link is kept to one clause and does not claim direct descent, since Metroid Wiki presents that as background inference. Pirate Command as a Knight area comes from the Metroid Wiki Knight locations list. The Lord's 'Phazon Beam' attack from the infobox is rendered generically as orbs of Phazon. The Nova Beam plus X-Ray Visor method comes from wiki body text and is applied to the late-crisis Homeworld Knights only. The Olympus and Norion narrative is kept to one line each. Phazite is not explained.

entries.comment: Prime 3: Korakk Beast and the Pirate Hussars
entries.content:
The Korakk is an armored beast that the Space Pirates prize as a cavalry mount. Its Phazite armor "will repel most damage." Its belly is occasionally vulnerable but guarded from all sides; the inside of its mouth and the tip of its tongue hold sensitive nerve clusters whose injury can briefly incapacitate it; and a nerve ending in its tail can be strained by grappling, but only while the tail is extended. A Korakk emits Phazon energy through its feet and tongue.

Pirate Hussars are its riders, "unusually brave for Space Pirates, willing to ride the deadly Korakk beast into combat." Each carries a Phazon Energy Lance, "deadly at any range," that fires bolts of Phazon energy and swings like a sword; otherwise a Hussar is no hardier than an ordinary Pirate trooper. Hussar and mount share what the logbook calls "a strange bond." A Korakk guards its rider with its life, and "If a Hussar is slain, his Korakk will fight to avenge his death."

During the Phazon crisis (Metroid Prime 3: Corruption) Samus met a lone Hussar, the only one she encountered, mounted on its Korakk in the Jousting Field of Bryyo Thorn Jungle. The beast stayed largely passive while its rider fought. When Samus killed the Hussar, the Korakk went berserk: it rammed her, hurled Phazon energy and seized her with its tongue until she wrenched free. Shots to the tongue as it lashed out stunned the beast, letting her roll beneath it in Morph Ball form and bomb its belly; after enough blasts it reared up and bared its underside to Ice Missiles and Hypermode fire, and she killed it.

The Korakk's death opened the way to the Leviathan Shield Generator in the Thorn Jungle, one of the two generators shielding Bryyo's Leviathan Seed. Its Phazite is the same Phazon-derived armor worn by the Berserker Knights and Commando Pirates Samus fought elsewhere in the crisis.
entries.notes: 319 words. This fills the 'Korakk Beast ... recorded separately' promise in Creatures: Fauna of Bryyo. The Korakk and Hussar logbook lines are quoted verbatim from Metroid Wiki. Both entries give the first location as 'Bryyo Thorn Jungle - Jousting Field'. 'Guard the Hussars with their lives' comes from the Metroid Wiki article intro, not the logbook, so it is paraphrased rather than quoted. 'The Korakk dies, so the Hussar dies too' is uncited on Metroid Wiki and was left out. That Samus met only one Hussar comes from Metroid Wiki. The fight details (passive until the rider dies, tongue grab, stun by shooting the tongue, Morph Ball bombs under the belly, rearing to expose it, Ice Missiles and Hypermode) come from the Metroid Wiki battle section. The task's 'Phazon venting' is rendered as the logbook's 'emits Phazon energy through its feet and tongue'. The Leviathan Shield Generator as 'one of two generators needed to shield the Bryyo leviathan' comes from the Bryyo Thorn Jungle page. No size or species description was available, so none is given. Space_Pirate_Data is listed only because existing Prime 3 entries cite it; this entry's facts do not depend on it.

entries.comment: Prime 3: Defense Drone (Elysian guardian of the Boost Ball)
entries.content:
The Defense Drone is an Elysian security machine, one of the Chozo-made mechanoids of SkyTown on Elysia. Its logbook states that it "is used to secure key areas within SkyTown." Its armor is immune to small-arms fire. Three externally mounted antennae feed its optic array, and destroying all of them overloads the array and leaves the machine briefly vulnerable. Its Control Unit is also vulnerable but must be exposed before it can be targeted.

During the Phazon crisis (Metroid Prime 3: Corruption) a Defense Drone guarded the Boost Ball in Ballista Storage. Unlike the Elysians bound to Pirate service, it showed no sign of Phazon corruption, which suggests the Space Pirates never reached the room; it attacked Samus all the same. As she approached the Boost Ball, a cage lowered her into the chamber. The Drone fought with missiles, a large plasma ball, leaping shock waves and later homing bombs. Samus shot down its three antennae, working fast because a damaged antenna regrew if the others stood too long; with the Drone stunned, she used the Grapple Lasso to pry open its head and expose the core, then struck it with Ice Missiles and Hypermode fire whenever its shielding slid back. The machine repeatedly resealed itself and regrew its antennae, and dense smoke filled the room as it neared destruction.

With Ghor and Helios, the Defense Drone was one of the three great guardians Samus faced on Elysia.
entries.notes: 238 words, inside the requested 200-250. The logbook is quoted or paraphrased from Metroid Wiki: 'used to secure key areas within SkyTown', antennas tied to the optic array, the Control Unit must be exposed, armor 'immune to small-arms fire'. The first location 'SkyTown, Elysia - Ballista Storage' comes from the logbook. 'Suggests the Pirates never reached the room' is a Metroid Wiki inference ('the room may not have been explored by Space Pirates') that the task asked for; it is kept as 'suggests' and can be cut if strict no-speculation is enforced. The Chozo origin follows Metroid Wiki ('The Elysian was a creation of the Chozo'). The 'three great guardians' line matches the existing Prime 3: Elysia and SkyTown entry and rests on the Metroid Wiki Elysia page's 'three main bosses, Ghor, Defense Drone, and Helios', reworded to avoid meta language. The entry deliberately does not say Samus recovered the Boost Ball afterward (owned by Equipment: Boost Ball, Spider Ball and Spider Magnet) and does not retell the Helios or Ghor fights.

result.research_notes:
The existing entries were checked first. Berserkers are mentioned in passing in Prime 3: Norion, Prime 3: GFS Olympus, Prime 3: Ghor and Prime 3: Gandrayda (Gandrayda's Phazon-charged Berserker Knight form), and the new entry agrees with all of them. The Korakk Beast was promised as 'recorded separately' in Creatures: Fauna of Bryyo, and the new entry fills that. The Defense Drone appears in Prime 3: Elysia and SkyTown ('three great guardians') and in Equipment: Boost Ball ('recovered it in SkyTown after destroying a Defense Drone'). The new entry avoids repeating the Boost Ball recovery line. Creatures: Fauna of Elysia mentions a Steamlord exposed by X-Ray in Ballista Storage, which does not conflict.

Verbatim logbook text came from Metroid Wiki for the Berserker Lord, Korakk Beast, Pirate Hussar and Defense Drone. The Berserker Knight logbook was available only in segments ('driven by battle lust' quoted; the rest paraphrased). The Metroid Wiki 'Metroid Prime 3: Corruption Logbook' page is incomplete: it covers only the Galactic Federation and Bryyo sections and does not have these entries. action=raw is 403. The breezewiki mirror of Wikitroid is blocked by Anubis, and Wikitroid was not fetched.

Two details rest only on Wikitroid text quoted in WebSearch snippets: the Turbine Chamber being in eastern SkyTown, and a Knight breaking through a wall at Transit Station 0205 in Pirate Command. Both were left out or generalized. The Turbine Chamber Lord and first Theronian Bomb component are confirmed on the Metroid Wiki Metroid Prime 3 page and in the Berserker Lord rewards.

Three tensions with canon scope:
- The 'guard the Hussars with their lives' line comes from the Metroid Wiki intro, not the logbook. It is paraphrased.
- The idea that the Defense Drone's lack of corruption means Pirates never reached Ballista Storage is a wiki inference. The task requested it, so it is kept with 'suggests'.
- 'Highest level of corruption' was paraphrased so the banned word 'level' stays out of content.

Order 100 matches the other Prime 3 entries. Each entry uses the game title once.
sources_consulted: WebSearch snippets citing metroid.fandom.com/wiki/Turbine_Chamber and metroid.fandom.com/wiki/Transit_Station_0205 (not fetched; used only for corroboration)
